papers.title: Data-Driven Conservation Laws for Newtonian Systems: Physics-Informed Neural Networks and Eisenhart-Duval Geometry
papers.abstract: We introduce a Physics-Informed Neural Network approach for the data-driven reconstruction of the symmetries and conservation laws of Newtonian dynamical systems, based on the geometrization of the dynamics through the Eisenhart-Duval lift. Within the Eisenhart-Duval lift, the symmetry conditions reduce to the linear Killing or Conformal Killing equations of the extended metric. We combine a Hamiltonian neural network, which reconstructs the potential function from the data, with a random-feature neural network, which solves the symmetry conditions for the collineations of the extended geometry. From the learned vector fields we construct the Lie algebra and, through Noether's theorem, the corresponding conserved quantities, while the derivation of the curvature invariants for the extended geometry provide allow us to perform an independent consistency test. We apply the method to the one-dimensional Ermakov-Pinney equation and to the one-dimensional harmonic oscillator, with and without a quartic perturbation, by using different level of noise in the phase-space data. For the Ermakov-Pinney equation, the three Killing vectors of the flat extended plane, and the corresponding nonlocal conservation laws, are recovered for, while for the harmonic oscillator, the ten conformal Killing vectors which form the $so(3,2)$ Lie algebra are determined for noise levels up to $10\%$. When the quartic term is added, the broken symmetries are identified as approximate symmetries.

papers.title: Hamiltonian dynamics with nonconservative forces on extended phase space: An analytical mechanics derivation
papers.abstract: This note derives the full Hamiltonian equations of motion on extended phase space for nonconservative and/or nonautonomous dynamical systems, with particular attention given to the momentum coordinate and generalized force associated with time. Time reparameterization is also considered, clarifying when it does or does not preserve Hamiltonian structure. The analytical mechanics framework is used throughout, with all developments formulated in terms of arbitrary symplectic coordinates; the main developments are not predicated on a Lagrangian description.

papers.title: Topological phases and scattering protected by projective chiral symmetry
papers.abstract: The bulk-boundary correspondence states that topological properties of a bulk material guarantee the existence of protected edge modes, oftentimes associated with the attractive property of backscattering immunity. In this Letter, we consider a time reversal invariant classical system with both translation and chiral, or sublattice, symmetries. We show that when these two symmetries anti-commute, the material exhibits a topological phase protected by the same invariant as type D topological superconductors. We realize such a system experimentally and observe the existence of the associated edge modes in an acoustic network. Our measurements are in excellent agreement with theoretical predictions from discrete lattice models. Finally, we show that these edge modes are immune to backscattering for perturbations consisting in two subsequent identical defects.

papers.title: Conductance scaling in nanopore arrays: disentangling roles of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry
papers.abstract: The scaling of electrical conductance with the number of nanopores, $N$, in an array is of fundamental importance for applications in membrane separation and ion transport across biological membranes, and has been the subject of longstanding disagreement in the field. Combining finite element calculations with theory, we resolve this disagreement for pores with negligible surface charge by showing that two previously conflicting predictions are each correct in their own limiting reservoir geometry: cuboidal reservoirs commensurate with the interpore spacing, for which the conductance scales linearly with $N$, and infinite reservoirs, for which the scaling is sublinear in $N$ for closely spaced pores. We show the transition between these limits with increasing reservoir size and, for infinite reservoirs, we show that a simple analytical model from electrical contact theory is mathematically equivalent to an existing point-charge capacitance model for nanopore arrays and validate its applicability against finite element and method-of-moments calculations. Using this model, we derive a characteristic coupling length, $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$, the interpore spacing at which the array conductance reaches $95\%$ of that of the same number of independent pores. $\ell_\mathrm{c,95}$ scales linearly with pore diameter $d$, and grows with $N$ as $\sim\log N$ for linear arrays and $\sim\sqrt{N}$ for square arrays, so that pore coupling persists to surprisingly large separations in large arrays. Our work provides a general framework for predicting nanopore array conductance as a function of pore arrangement and reservoir geometry, of importance to nanofluidics research and the targeted design of functional devices.

papers.title: Prestatability in the Macroscopic Limit
papers.abstract: We examine whether the variables required for a future macroscopic description of a given physical system can themselves be stated in advance. Representing macroscopic descriptions as coarse-grainings of a fixed microscopic phase space, we distinguish formal prestatability, concerning the existence of an effective complete vocabulary of admissible macroscopic distinctions, from dynamical prestatability, concerning whether the future relevance of those distinctions is decidable. Both obstructions disappear for finite microscopic state spaces. In the infinite limit, exhaustive formal prestatability can fail, while a restricted predictive architecture may remain formally pre-statable. We construct such an architecture and show that, under universal dynamics, the future relevance of a candidate variable is equivalent to the halting problem. Thus a fixed microscopic phase space can support macroscopic descriptions whose future variables are not fully pre-statable.

papers.title: On deep squeezing or cooling a parametric resonator using feedback
papers.abstract: Here we analyze ways to achieve deep subthreshold squeezing or cooling of fluctuations in a parametric resonator enhanced by a lock-in amplifier feedback loop. The main advance and novelty of this paper is that we analyzed the full impact of this feedback on the response of the parametric resonator to an ac drive or to additive noise. Due to this feedback, the dynamics of the parametric resonator becomes more complex and, in addition to a saddle-node bifurcation (SNB), a Hopf bifurcation (HB) at the instability threshold can also occur. We calculate the phase-dependent amplification gain in the response of the resonator to an added ac signal with three independent techniques: approximately using the averaging method (AM) or the harmonic balance method (HBM), and more precisely using Floquet theory (FT) and Green's functions. The HB was predicted by the AM, FT, and a modified version of the HBM that takes into account quasi-periodicity. In our analysis of fluctuations, we were able to calculate the noise spectral density and the squeezing or cooling of fluctuations using Fourier techniques and FT. Deamplification and cooling occur near the HB, whereas deep squeezing and heating occur near a SNB. Furthermore, we show that there is an optimal amount of parametric pumping and feedback to reach the strongest cooling. The theoretical framework presented here is general and could be applied to a wide range of physical implementations.

papers.title: New approach to approximate analytical solutions for a harmonic oscillator subject to combined linear and nonlinear damping
papers.abstract: We introduce a new approach to deriving approximate analytical solutions of a harmonic oscillator damped by purely nonlinear, or combinations of linear and nonlinear damping forces. Our approach is based on choosing a suitable trial solution, i.e. an ansatz, which is the product of the time-dependent amplitude and the oscillatory (trigonometric) function with a reduced frequency (due solely to linear damping) and an initial phase shift (due to both linear and nonlinear damping) compared to the undamped case. We derive the amplitude decay equation using the connection of the energy dissipation rate with the power of the total damping force. By matching our ansatz to the initial conditions, we obtain equations for its initial amplitude and initial phase. We demonstrate the validity of our approach for quadratic damping, a combination of linear and quadratic damping, and finally a combination of linear, quadratic, and Coulomb damping. For pure quadratic damping and for a combination of linear and quadratic damping, we compare our approximate analytical solutions with the corresponding numerical solutions and find that they describe the oscillator dynamics well in the regime of weak to moderately strong damping. For the combination of all three types of damping, our solutions agree well with the numerical solutions until the last half-period or the last few half-periods of the motion (primarily depending on the strength of the Coulomb damping). In addition, we show how to use our solutions to determine damping constants from given displacement vs. time data, demonstrating that they can be applied to the analysis of experiments.

papers.title: Tuning Plasma Frequency of Nested Wire Media
papers.abstract: We study nested wire media possessing $C_6$ and $C_4$ rotational symmetries whose plasma frequencies can be controlled through breathing deformation. Numerical simulations reveal tunability exceeding $80\%$ and $60\%$ for the considered $C_6$ and $C_4$ breathing geometries, respectively. To describe these structures, we develop an analytical model based on the local field approach within the thin-wire approximation, which confirms the high tunability of the studied wire structures. We also propose an approximation for dense wire media. The developed framework is applicable to the general case of nested wire structures -- wire media with an arbitrary parallelogram lattice and multiple wires per unit cell.

papers.title: Generalization of Rayleigh's high-frequency theory for the 2D Helmholtz equation in a half-space subject to a radiation condition at infinity and a Dirichlet condition on a 1D periodically-uneven boundary
papers.abstract: The 2D Helmholtz equation, radiation condition and Dirichlet boundary condition, are the translation, in mathematical terms, of (at least) three physical 2D problems for the prediction of the total scalar wavefield on one side of an impenetrable 1D periodically uneven boundary when: a) a plane TE electromagnetic wave propagating in the vacuum strikes the boundary the other side of which is occupied by a perfectly-conducting medium, b) a plane SH elastic elastic wave strikes a rigid boundary, c) a plane acoustic wave strikes a pressure-release boundary. The first attempt to solve such problems in a non-heuristic manner was made by Lord Rayleigh (in his book, 'The Theory of Sound' which appeared in 1896). My task will be to revisit Rayleigh's theory of diffraction by a sinusoidal-shaped, impenetrable boundary, and more specifically, his perturbation method for obtaining a mathematically-explicit solution to the diffraction problem in the high-frequency regime. In so doing, I shall correct and generalize Rayleigh's method to obtain solutions for arbitrary angles of incidence as well as for 1D periodic impenetrable boundaries of quite-general shape.
